title: Dilations and Similar Figures
seo_title: Geometry Dilations and Similar Figures Worksheets (TEKS G.7A)
standard_text: G.7A apply the definition of similarity in terms of a dilation to identify similar figures and their proportional sides and the congruent corresponding angles
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.7A: dilations from the origin and other centers, scale factors and similar polygons. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Dilations multiply distances by k and keep angles.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A dilation with scale factor k multiplies every distance from the center by k.
  • k > 1 enlarges; 0 < k < 1 reduces.
  • Figures are similar if a dilation (and rigid moves) maps one onto the other: angles are congruent and sides are proportional.

Examples

Example

Dilate (4, −6) by 1/2 from the origin

multiply both coordinates

Answer: (2, −3)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the scale factorMultiply, do not add.
Writing the ratio upside downImage ÷ pre-image.
Thinking angles changeDilations keep angles.

faq.a: Apply the definition of similarity in terms of a dilation to identify similar figures and their proportional sides and the congruent corresponding angles.

items.q: Point A(−6, −2) is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × −6, 2 × −2) = (−12, −4).

items.q: A figure is dilated by a scale factor of 52. Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: A scale factor greater than 1 makes the image larger. An enlargement.

items.q: A dilation centered at the origin maps A(−7, 5) to A′(−21, 15). What is the scale factor?
items.e: Divide an image coordinate by the original: −21 ÷ (−7) = 3.

items.e: Find the step from C to A: (−8, 6). Multiply it by 12: (−4, 3). Add it to C: (−5, 2).

items.q: Quadrilateral LBEJ ~ quadrilateral SYDQ. EJ = 2, DQ = 6 and LB = 6. Find SY.
items.e: The scale factor from LBEJ to SYDQ is 6 ÷ 2 = 3. SY = 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q: Quadrilateral PJMY ~ quadrilateral SQGD. YP = 18, DS = 45 and MY = 6. Find GD.
items.e: The scale factor from PJMY to SQGD is 45 ÷ 18 = 52. GD = 52 × 6 = 15.

items.q: Quadrilateral DKXH ~ quadrilateral AQLZ. HD = 3, ZA = 6 and KX = 12. Find QL.
items.e: The scale factor from DKXH to AQLZ is 6 ÷ 3 = 2. QL = 2 × 12 = 24.

items.q: Quadrilateral JLUY ~ quadrilateral DVMZ. LU = 10, VM = 20 and UY = 6. Find MZ.
items.e: The scale factor from JLUY to DVMZ is 20 ÷ 10 = 2. MZ = 2 × 6 = 12.

items.q: Quadrilateral PJAU ~ quadrilateral LMCQ. PJ = 4, LM = 10 and UP = 24. Find QL.
items.e: The scale factor from PJAU to LMCQ is 10 ÷ 4 = 52. QL = 52 × 24 = 60.

items.q: Quadrilateral EPVX ~ quadrilateral HFYD. VX = 2, YD = 4 and EP = 8. Find HF.

items.q: A side of length 11 becomes 55 after a dilation. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = image ÷ original = 55 ÷ 11 = 5.

items.q: A side of length 21 becomes 14 after a dilation. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = image ÷ original = 14 ÷ 21 = 23.

items.q: A polygon has area 20 square units. It is dilated by a scale factor of 4. What is the area of the image?
items.e: Area is multiplied by the square of the scale factor: (4)² × 20 = 16 × 20 = 320 square units.

items.q: Two similar figures have corresponding sides in the ratio 2 : 7. What is the ratio of their areas?
items.e: The ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of sides: 2² : 7² = 4 : 49.

items.q: A polygon has area 60 square units. It is dilated by a scale factor of 32. What is the area of the image?

items.q: A segment of length 20 is dilated by a scale factor of 52. How long is the image?

items.q: On a map, 1 inch represents 10 miles. Two cities are 3 inches apart on the map. How far apart are they?
items.e: Multiply by the scale: 3 × 10 = 30 miles.

items.q: A model ship is built at a scale of 1 : 100. The model is 2 ft long. How long is the real ship?
items.e: Every real length is 100 times the model length: 100 × 2 = 200 ft.

items.q: A 8-inch pizza and a 12-inch pizza are similar circles. How many times as much pizza is the larger one?
items.e: Areas scale by the square of the ratio: (12 ÷ 8)² = 144 ÷ 64 = 94.

items.q: Carlos enlarges a 4 in. by 6 in. photo so that the short side is 8 in. How long is the long side?
items.e: The scale factor is 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Long side = 2 × 6 = 12 in.

items.q: A 12-inch pizza and a 16-inch pizza are similar circles. How many times as much pizza is the larger one?
items.e: Areas scale by the square of the ratio: (16 ÷ 12)² = 256 ÷ 144 = 169.

items.q: A rectangular screen 16 in. wide is dilated by a scale factor of 32 to make a larger screen. By what factor does the screen's area increase?
